summary: Conservative screening policy for Community Beta. Automatic publication requires a confident Neutral image and a clean result from every text dictionary; every other outcome, uncertainty included, routes to a human.

image.classNamesRationale: The exact NSFW_CLASSES set exported by nsfwjs@4.3.0, in the canonical order the model's output vector uses positionally. A vector of any other length, or a class-name set that does not match this list exactly, is invalid output and routes to review.
image.neutralPassMinimumRationale: Automatic publication requires a confident Neutral rather than merely the highest-scoring class. The benign reference image measured during story review scored Neutral 0.9063, so 0.85 leaves real headroom for ordinary fashion photography while still demanding clear model confidence. Anything at or below this value routes to review.
image.unsafeAggregateMaximumRationale: A confident Neutral alone is not enough to publish. Neutral 0.86 with Porn 0.13 clears the Neutral gate and sits below the per-class block threshold, so without this third condition a vector carrying thirteen percent unsafe mass would reach automatic publication. Pass therefore also requires the sum of the unsafeClasses probabilities to be strictly below 0.10. The benign reference image sums Hentai 0.0421 and Porn 0.0015 to 0.0436, so an ordinary fashion photograph keeps better than a factor of two in hand, while any vector where unsafe mass is a real share of the distribution falls to review.
image.unsafeClassesRationale: Sexy is deliberately absent. On a fashion product, swimwear, lingerie and eveningwear score Sexy legitimately, and blocking them automatically would be the dominant false-positive source. A high Sexy probability still cannot reach pass, because it necessarily pushes Neutral below neutralPassMinimum, so such an image is withheld and shown to a human instead of being blocked outright. Drawing is not an unsafe class at all.
image.unsafeBlockMinimumRationale: The benign reference image scored Porn 0.0015 and Hentai 0.0421, so 0.35 sits an order of magnitude above the observed benign ceiling while staying below the 0.5 plurality point. A clearly unsafe image blocks; an ambiguous one falls through to review. Block and review both leave the post unpublished, so a low block threshold costs a moderator nothing beyond queue priority.
image.probabilitySumToleranceRationale: The model output is already softmaxed and measured 0.99999992 on the reference input. A tolerance of 0.001 is three orders of magnitude above that float32 accumulation error and still small enough to catch a truncated, padded, or otherwise corrupted vector, which a permissive tolerance would wave through.
image.boundaryDispositionRationale: Comparisons are strict. A probability exactly at a threshold has not passed it, so pass requires Neutral strictly greater than neutralPassMinimum and block requires an unsafe class strictly greater than unsafeBlockMinimum. Both boundaries therefore resolve to review, which is the fail-closed direction on each side.
openQuestions: An aggregate BLOCK threshold was considered and deliberately not set. A vector such as Hentai 0.30 with Porn 0.30 sums to 0.60 of unsafe mass yet clears neither single-class block rule, so it routes to review rather than block. That is safe, because review keeps the post unpublished, and it is a moderator queue-load question rather than a fail-open. Choosing a number for it without corpus evidence is exactly the measurement Story 6.2b exists to make, so it is left open here on purpose rather than guessed.

text.categoriesRationale: Six categories that a reviewed term list can actually be graded against. They subsume the two categories the Story 6.1 engine shipped: its profanity list maps to profanity, and its safety list splits across self_harm, violence and harassment, which is the distinction a moderator needs and the flat safety label hid.
text.severityDispositionRationale: No matched term can reach pass, so low and medium deliberately share the review disposition. The grade is still recorded because it drives moderator queue priority and because Story 6.2b measures the false-positive rate per severity; collapsing them into one level would destroy that signal without changing a single publication outcome.
text.unscreenableLocaleDispositionRationale: A locale this policy holds no dictionary for cannot be cleared by silence. The Story 6.1 engine already emits locale_unscreenable for that case and refuses the post; this policy keeps that behavior rather than rebuilding it.
text.allDictionariesAlwaysRunRationale: Every language list runs against every submission regardless of the declared locale, so a client-controlled locale field cannot be used to bypass another language's terms.

scripts.rationale: All seven enabled languages are written in Latin script, so Common and Inherited cover punctuation, digits and combining marks. Observed script is determined by deterministic Unicode inspection; no probabilistic language detection runs anywhere in this policy. Mixed or unsupported scripts are the confusable-substitution attack surface, so both fail closed to a human.

limits.rationale: Per field, because the screener is field-aware and the public contract already enforces both ceilings: communityPostCaptionSchema caps a caption at 280 characters and communityPostAltTextSchema caps alt text at 200. Screening a longer value would mean normalising input the API had no business accepting. Capping the number of canonical representations and their combined length stops crafted input from amplifying normalization work without limit.

text.listsRationale: One reviewed list plus one allow list per enabled language, covering the seven languages the ten enabled Community Beta locales map to. Every entry carries source, version and licence, and a list missing any of the three fails startup. Story 6.2b replaces these repository-owned provenance records with the pinned upstream lists it vendors.
openQuestions: The term lists were authored on a four-level severity scale and this policy has three, so critical was merged into high. No publication outcome changes, because both blocked. What is lost is ordering inside the block tier: a hate slur and ordinary strong profanity are now indistinguishable once both map to high, so a moderator queue cannot rank one above the other and a per-severity measurement cannot separate them. Story 6.2b measures the false-positive rate per severity and should decide then whether the fourth level earns its place.

reasonCodes.rationale: Stable codes shared by the image adapter, the text screener and the durable pipeline, so a persisted reason means the same thing on every branch. The disposition recorded against each code is its floor: text_policy_match escalates to block when the matched term severity maps to block, and no code here can ever yield pass. text_input_truncated is its own code because it describes a different failure from the others: input past a per-field ceiling, or input that exhausted maxExpandedCharacters before every canonical representation was built, means part of the text was never screened at all. A clean result over a partial reading is not a clean result, so it fails closed to review under its own name instead of borrowing one that would misdescribe it. image_disposition_conflict covers a screener that reports passed true beside a refusing disposition: the two halves of its own verdict contradict each other, so the safe reading is the refusing one, and without a named code that case held a post with an empty reason list. text_clean sits in cleanCodes rather than in this table, because every code under image and text must resolve to review or block and the schema makes pass unrepresentable there. It still has to be named: a screener that states a clean verdict is auditable, whereas one that merely returns an empty reason list is indistinguishable from a screener that refused without explaining itself.
